reflections.title: "All Things Are Possible"

reflect.text: When the troubled father approached Jesus, he said, "If You can do anything, have compassion on us." Jesus showed him that the question was never about whether the Lord was able. As Charles Spurgeon noted, the father had put his "if" in the wrong place. Christ has both the power and the willingness to help. The real question is whether we will trust Him.

Too often, we treat constant doubt and spiritual weakness as normal. Our unbelief becomes the main obstacle that holds us back, especially when we face an urgent problem. Yet even small faith can accomplish great things when it rests upon the living Savior. A tiny seed can draw life from the ground, and a narrow channel can receive the water of the ocean.

Instead of focusing on your struggles or the size of your faith, turn your eyes toward the faithfulness of Jesus. He invites us to leave our fear behind and step into the steady assurance He provides. All things are possible for the person who trusts in Him.

questions: In what areas of your life are you tempted to question God's power rather than trusting His promises?
How can focusing on Jesus' faithfulness help you move past lingering doubts?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, forgive us when we question Your power and willingness to help. Teach us to rest our confidence completely in You, especially during difficult times. Strengthen our trust so that fear no longer rules our hearts. Amen.

reflections.title: "Help My Unbelief"

reflect.text: Long, exhausting trials can wear down our spirits and make our struggles seem much larger than God's power. When the father cried out, "I do believe; help my unbelief," he did not pretend to have perfect confidence. He brought his honest weakness straight to Jesus. The Lord welcomes our sincerity and does not turn away from those who admit their doubts and fears.

True faith is not merely knowing facts about Jesus; it is trusting Him personally with our lives. The power of faith does not depend on how strong our feelings are, but on the Savior we hold onto. Even weak, trembling faith receives Christ's mercy because His strength is far greater than our human limits.

When we try to keep control of our circumstances, anxiety grows and our prayers can become hesitant. Jesus invites us to surrender that control and ask Him for the help we need. As we remember His past faithfulness and seek Him in prayer and Scripture, He gently grows our faith and gives us peace.

questions: What doubts or worries do you need to confess honestly to Jesus today?
How does knowing that Jesus accepts weak faith encourage you when trials feel overwhelming?
reflections.prayer: Dear Jesus, we bring our small and wavering faith to You today. Forgive us for trying to keep control of outcomes that belong in Your hands. Please help our unbelief, quiet our anxious thoughts, and teach us to depend fully on Your grace. Amen.

D10.work: A Prayer to Help Us Believe

reflections.title: Bring Him to Me

reflect.text: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai, his face shone with such blinding brightness that the people were afraid, and he had to wear a veil. But when Jesus came down from the mountain of transfiguration, the crowd was not driven away by fear. Instead, they ran toward Him in wonder. God's law shows us our guilt, but Jesus reveals God's tender grace and love, drawing sinners into His welcoming presence.

At the bottom of the mountain, a brokenhearted father found that the disciples were powerless to heal his suffering child. Yet Jesus gave the simple command: "Bring him to Me." Our loved ones, especially our children, can bring great joy or profound sorrow into our lives. When we see our complete helplessness against the pain and brokenness of this world, the Lord is teaching us to turn directly to Him.

No circumstance or person is hopeless as long as Jesus lives. Sometimes God allows us to reach the end of our own strength so that we will run to the Great Physician. We must never stop bringing our burdens and our families to Him in earnest prayer.

questions: How does the welcoming kindness of Jesus encourage you to approach Him rather than hide in fear?
Who in your life seems beyond help, and how can you bring them to Jesus in prayer today?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for drawing us to Yourself with kindness and mercy. When we feel powerless to help the people we love, remind us to bring every burden directly to You. Give us persistence in prayer and steady hope in Your unfailing love. Amen.
